description: Brief → one decision per layer → an ADR per decision → a walking skeleton through all of them → the trade-offs and what was left out on purpose.
A tiny end-to-end implementation that exercises every architectural layer. It proves the decisions fit together before features are added.
The data shaped for one screen: only the fields the UI renders, already formatted. Produced by the BFF.
Server data serialized into the HTML (`<script type="application/json">`) so the client hydrates without fetching it again.
JSON with `<` escaped as `\u003c`, so data cannot close the surrounding `<script>` tag while `JSON.parse` still returns the original value.
The server, acting as a gateway, received an invalid response from an upstream service. The right status when the BFF's backend fails.
An ADR whose claims are verified against the code by a test (the rendering API used, the import boundaries, the state libraries), so the record cannot silently drift from reality.
What was deliberately left out, ideally with the trigger that would justify adding it ("TanStack Query with the first client-side mutation").
